label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl, models/big_rock.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: Every view reads as the valve wheel the brief asks for. Front and back show a round rim with five spokes and a hub. Side, top and below views show a thin disc with the stem through its centre. The rim is built from about twelve flat segments, which is normal for a GoldSrc prop. Nothing sticks out and nothing is missing.

M2.reason: It measures 33 x 32 across against the 32 asked. That is 3.1% off, inside the 15% allowed. Its 12.2 depth is a sensible stem length.

M3.reason: It has a rim, five evenly spaced spokes, a hub with a hex nut on the front face and a stem running out the back. These are the parts a valve wheel needs, each in its place and the right shape.

M4.reason: The rim, spokes and hub are painted red, the rim's edges and one worn arc are bare grey steel, and the stem is rusted brown. The brief asks for red paint worn to steel at the rim, and that is what it has.

M5.reason: The wear is there but looks mechanical. Bare steel runs as an even grey band along the whole outer edge of the rim. The one bigger worn patch, at about 1 to 4 o'clock in the front view, is flat grey with hard ends on the segment lines, so it reads as a separately coloured piece rather than worn paint. A small V-shaped notch shows at 12 o'clock on the rim in the front and back views, where the ring's two ends meet. The red has fine dark speckle but no chips or scuffs where hands would grip.

M6.reason: In the lineup it is B. Its low-res texture, flat shading and plain construction sit alongside big_rock, testsphere and gib_legbone without standing out, so a player would take it for one of the game's props.

M7.reason: It stands upright with the hub nut on the front and the stem going back, as a wheel on a valve body would. It is centred in every view and nothing looks offset from its origin.

M8.reason: SMAK's check passes, and nothing is open, inside out or floating. But it has 392 triangles against a median of 62 for Half-Life's props of this size. The limit is twice the median, 124, and this is more than three times that. Most of the extra triangles are probably in the many-sided spokes and stem.
